detail:
MedlinePlus describes complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) as a chronic pain condition that usually affects an arm or a leg, most often after an injury, surgery, stroke, or heart attack, with pain that is more severe or longer lasting than expected from the original event. Sources divide CRPS into type 1, which follows an illness or injury without a confirmed distinct nerve injury, and type 2, which follows a distinct nerve injury; most cases described are type 1.

MedlinePlus notes that symptoms can include continuous burning or throbbing pain, sensitivity to touch or cold, swelling of the painful area, changes in skin temperature and color, changes in skin texture, altered hair and nail growth, joint stiffness and swelling, muscle weakness, and decreased ability to move the affected body part. Clinicians usually diagnose CRPS from medical history, symptoms, and a physical exam, and tests such as bone scans, nerve studies, or imaging are sometimes used to help rule out other conditions rather than to confirm CRPS on their own.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about complex regional pain syndrome symptoms and diagnosis.
summary: MedlinePlus describes CRPS as chronic limb pain after an injury or other event that exceeds what the event would explain, with symptoms that can include burning pain, sensitivity, swelling, and skin changes.
takeaways: CRPS pain is described as disproportionate to the triggering event
symptoms can include burning pain, swelling, and skin color changes
diagnosis rests mainly on history, symptoms, and physical examination
title: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS): when pain persists after an injury
